newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Opposing Afghan factions vie for OIC seat.
newsitem.headline: Opposing Afghan factions vie for OIC seat.

text.p: Officials from both sides in the Afghan conflict were in the Indonesian capital of Jakarta vying for Kabul's seat at the Organisation of the Islamic Conference (OIC), officials said on Monday.
"Both sides are jockeying for the seat," a conference official said.
Senior officials who met to set the agenda at IOC headquarters in Jeddah last month decided not to invite a delegation from Kabul because they could not agree on who should represent Afghanistan.
Conference officials said the Afghan issue might be raised from the floor during one of the plenary sessions.
The hardline Islamic Taleban militia seized Kabul on September 27. Forces loyal to ousted President Burhanuddin Rabbani and ethnic Uzbek leader Rashid Dostum are trying to retake the city.
"The ministerial conference will try to find a way out of this problem," Indonesian Foreign Minister Ali Alatas said earlier.
